newsitem.title: USA: U.S.-China economic conference set for next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-China economic conference set for next week.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin announced on Wednesday that he and Chinese Finance Minister Liu Zhongli will co-host a U.S.-China Joint Economic Commission meeting on Nov 18-19 in Washington.
They will discuss economic issues and will include talks on the trade imbalance in China's favor, financial market reform and customs cooperation and tax issues, Treasury said.

The U.S. delegation will include representatives from Treasury, the U.S. Trade Representative's office, the Council of Economic Advisors, State Department, Federal Reserve and the Securities and Exchange Commission.

The Chinese delegation will include members from the Ministry of Finance, the State Planning Commission, the Committee on Restructuring the Economy, the ministries of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, the People's Bank of China and the China Securities Regulatory Commission.

Trade is emerging as an especially contentious issue in relations with China. The deficit with China in August -- the most recently available month -- of $4.71 billion was the largest with any single trading partner, surpassing Japan.
A press conference is scheduled for Tuesday, Nov 19, at the conclusion of the two-day meeting.
